Premium Dry Herb Vaporizers

Experience cleaner, more flavorful sessions with our selection of dry herb vaporizers. Vaporizing heats your material below combustion temperatures, releasing active compounds as vapor rather than smoke. The result? Smoother hits, better flavor, and more efficient use of your herbs.

Benefits of Dry Herb Vaporizers

  • Cleaner Experience: No combustion means no smoke or tar
  • Enhanced Flavor: Taste the full terpene profile of your herbs
  • Efficiency: Extract more from less material
  • Discretion: Less odor than traditional smoking methods
  • Temperature Control: Customize your experience

Portable vs. Desktop Vaporizers

Portable vapes offer convenience and discretion for on-the-go use. Desktop vaporizers provide superior vapor quality and larger chambers for home sessions. Many users own both for different situations.

Temperature Guide

Lower temps (320-350°F) emphasize flavor and lighter effects. Medium temps (350-400°F) balance flavor and vapor production. Higher temps (400-430°F) produce thicker vapor and stronger effects. Start low and experiment to find your preference.

Dry Herb Vaporizers — FAQ

What's the difference between conduction and convection vaporizers?

Conduction vaporizers heat the chamber directly, which heats your material faster but can cause uneven heating. Convection vaporizers pass hot air through your material, providing more even heating, better flavor, and more efficient use — usually at a higher price point.

Are dry herb vaporizers better than smoking?

Vaporizers heat material below combustion temperature (~350–430°F), producing vapor instead of smoke. Users report smoother inhalation, cleaner flavor, and less odor compared to combustion. Many also prefer the precise temperature control for drawing out specific terpenes.

How often should I clean my dry herb vaporizer?

Clean the chamber and mouthpiece after every 5–10 sessions for optimal flavor. A quick brush-out after each bowl keeps the screen clear. Use isopropyl alcohol (91%+) for a deep clean once a month — never submerge electronic components.

Vape Pens — Buyer's Guide

Vape pens are compact vaporizers designed for discreet, on-the-go use. Most are pen-shaped for pocketability and use either pre-filled 510-thread cartridges or refillable tanks. They heat material below combustion, producing vapor instead of smoke.

What do the 510, 710, and 1100 mean?

These refer to thread standards for cartridge compatibility. 510 threads are the industry standard — most cartridges and batteries use this fitting. 710 and 1100 are less common alternative threadings used by specific brands.

Are vape pens better than smoking?

Vaporizing heats material below the 451°F combustion point, producing vapor that contains fewer particulates and no tar from burning plant matter. Users report smoother hits, less odor, and more efficient use of material compared to combustion.

How do I know when my cartridge is empty?

When draws become thin and lose flavor, the cartridge is near empty. Some pens have battery-indicator LEDs; others rely on visible oil level in the cartridge window. Replace or refill when flavor degrades noticeably.

What's the best temperature for a vape pen?

Low (320–360°F) preserves terpenes and flavor. Medium (360–400°F) balances flavor with vapor thickness. High (400–430°F) produces bigger clouds at the cost of flavor. Variable-voltage pens let you find your preference.

percolator-bongs:
Percolator Bongs & Perc Water Pipes

A percolator bong adds an extra stage of water filtration that breaks vapor into hundreds of tiny bubbles, cooling and smoothing every pull before it reaches you. That diffusion is the difference between a harsh, hot draw and the clean, effortless hit that premium glass is known for. If you have outgrown a basic beaker, a percolator water pipe is the single biggest upgrade you can make.

📖 Read: Percolator Bongs Guide 2026 →

How a percolator works

As you draw, vapor is forced through small slits, holes, or arms submerged in water. Each opening shears the smoke into smaller bubbles, and smaller bubbles mean more surface area in contact with the water — which means more cooling and more filtration of particulates. The more percolators (or the finer the slits), the smoother the result, though heavily diffused pieces require a little more lung power.

Types of percolators

  • Tree perc: multiple vertical arms with slits — excellent diffusion, a classic look.
  • Honeycomb perc: a flat disc of many small holes — maximum bubbles with low drag.
  • Showerhead perc: a vertical tube with slits at the base — reliable and easy to clean.
  • Matrix & turbine percs: grid and spinning designs that add a swirling visual effect.
  • Recycler percs: loop water through chambers for continuous filtration (see our recycler collection).

What to look for in a percolator bong

  • Glass thickness: 5mm to 9mm borosilicate resists cracks and thermal stress.
  • Perc count vs. airflow: more percs cool better but add drag — match it to how hard you like to pull.
  • Cleaning access: removable downstems and wider openings make multi-perc pieces far easier to maintain.
  • Base stability: a wide beaker or stand-up base keeps your investment safe on the table.

Keeping a percolator bong clean

Because percolators trap residue in their small openings, regular cleaning keeps airflow and flavor at their best. A quick rinse with a salt-and-isopropyl solution after a few sessions prevents buildup. Elevate your dab rig with high-quality quartz bangers. Quartz is the gold standard for dabbing—it heats evenly, retains temperature well, and provides the cleanest, most flavorful experience. Our selection includes various styles to match your rig and preferences.

Why Choose Quartz?

  • Pure Flavor: Quartz doesn't impart any taste to your dabs
  • Even Heating: Consistent temperature across the entire surface
  • Heat Retention: Holds temperature for longer sessions
  • Easy to Clean: Q-tip tech keeps quartz looking new
  • Visual Appeal: Watch your concentrate vaporize

Banger Styles

Standard bangers offer classic functionality. Flat-top bangers work with most carb caps. Slanted bangers direct concentrate to one side. Thermal bangers feature double-wall design for better heat retention. Terp slurpers maximize vaporization through unique airflow.

Joint Sizes & Angles

Match your banger to your rig's joint: 14mm and 18mm are most common. Choose 90-degree for straight-neck rigs or 45-degree for angled joints. Male bangers insert into female joints; female bangers fit over male joints.

Quartz Bangers & Nails — FAQ

What size quartz banger do I need?

Match your banger to your dab rig joint: measure the joint opening in millimeters (10mm, 14mm, or 18mm). Also note gender (male or female): if your rig has a socket, you need a male banger; if it has a stem, you need a female banger. Most modern rigs use 14mm male joints.

Flat top vs. round bottom banger — what's the difference?

Flat-top bangers sit parallel to your rig for better airflow and work with a wider range of carb caps. Round-bottom bangers maintain heat longer and create better vortex spin with terp pearls. Flat-top is the modern standard; round-bottom is preferred by some low-temp purists.

How thick should a quartz banger be?

2mm is standard. 3mm+ thick bangers retain heat longer but take longer to cool — favored for low-temp dabbing with terp pearls. 4mm+ is premium heavy-duty for commercial or heavy use. Thicker isn't always better; 2mm works fine for most dabbers.

How do I season a new quartz banger?

Heat the banger to red-hot with a torch, then dunk briefly in cold water. Repeat 3–5 times. This removes any manufacturing residue and stabilizes the quartz. Your banger will be flavor-neutral for the first dab.

Wax Vaporizers & Oil Vape Pens — FAQ

What's the difference between a wax vaporizer and an oil pen?

Wax vaporizers use a chamber with a coil or quartz cup to vaporize thicker concentrates (shatter, budder, wax, rosin). Oil vape pens use pre-filled or refillable cartridges designed for thinner oils. Wax vapes deliver bigger hits and more flavor; oil pens win on convenience and portability.

Are wax vaporizers better than dabbing?

For portability and convenience — yes. Modern wax vaporizers reach dabbing temperatures (450–600°F) in seconds without a torch, delivering near-dab-quality hits anywhere. Purists argue traditional rigs offer better flavor, but the gap has narrowed dramatically with premium e-rigs like Puffco.

How long does a wax vape battery last?

Portable wax vaporizers typically deliver 30–80 sessions per charge, depending on power draw. Charge time is 1–3 hours via USB-C. For heavy use, carry a spare battery or a charging case.

Can I use the same coil for different concentrates?

Yes, but different coils optimize different materials. Quartz coils deliver best flavor for premium waxes. Ceramic coils work well for most concentrates at lower cost. Swap coils when flavor degrades — usually after 2–4 weeks of regular use.

Dual-Use Vaporizers: Dry Herb & Concentrates

Get the best of both worlds with our dual-use vaporizers. These versatile devices handle both dry herb and concentrates, eliminating the need for multiple devices. Perfect for users who enjoy variety or want to try different consumption methods without investing in separate vaporizers.

Advantages of Dual-Use Vapes

  • Versatility: Switch between dry herb and concentrates
  • Cost Savings: One device for multiple materials
  • Travel-Friendly: Carry one device instead of two
  • Experimentation: Discover which consumption method you prefer

How Dual-Use Vaporizers Work

Most dual-use vapes include interchangeable chambers or pods—one optimized for dry herb with proper airflow, another designed for concentrates with appropriate heating elements. Some models feature hybrid chambers that can handle both with a single insert.

Tips for Best Results

Allow time between switching materials to avoid flavor contamination. Clean concentrate chambers more frequently to prevent residue buildup. Use different temperature settings for each material—concentrates typically require higher temperatures than dry herb.

Dual-Use Vaporizers — FAQ

What is a dual-use vaporizer?

A dual-use (or hybrid) vaporizer handles both dry herb and concentrates in the same device, usually through interchangeable chambers or pods. They're ideal for users who enjoy both material types and don't want to carry two separate devices.

How do you switch between herb and concentrate?

Most dual-use vapes use swappable atomizers or pods: one for herb (a ceramic or quartz-screened chamber), one for concentrate (a coil or cup). Changeover takes seconds. The device's temperature presets adjust automatically for each material.

Do dual-use vapes compromise performance?

Modern hybrids (XVAPE Fog Pro, Lookah Q7, Utillian series) match the performance of single-purpose devices at similar price points. Heat profiles, airflow, and battery life are optimized for each mode. Older or cheaper dual-use devices may underperform on one material.

What's the best dual-use vaporizer for beginners?

Look for a device with clear temperature presets (not variable voltage), a simple single-button interface, and swappable pods rather than rebuilt atomizers. Budget $80–150 for reliable performance; avoid devices under $50 unless they're a specific well-reviewed model.

Titanium & Ceramic Nails — FAQ

Titanium vs. ceramic nail — which is better?

Titanium heats quickly, holds heat well, and is virtually unbreakable — the most durable nail type. Downsides: metallic flavor for the first few uses (requires seasoning) and slower cooling. Ceramic offers the cleanest, most neutral flavor with no seasoning needed, but is more fragile and retains heat even longer than titanium.

Why did quartz replace titanium and ceramic?

Quartz bangers delivered better flavor and faster heat cycles, becoming the modern standard. Titanium and ceramic nails remain popular for specific use cases: titanium for rugged daily drivers that won't crack, ceramic for flavor purists who prefer extended low-temp sessions.

How do I season a new titanium nail?

Heat the nail red-hot with your torch, then dunk briefly in cold water. Repeat 3–5 times. This removes manufacturing residue and creates a stable oxide layer that eliminates the metallic taste. Your nail should then be flavor-neutral for all future dabs.

Can I use a carb cap with titanium or ceramic nails?

Yes — a carb cap improves low-temp vaporization on any nail material. Universal caps fit most titanium domeless nails; ceramic nails often ship with matching caps. For best results, use a cap with an airflow hole that directs vapor across the nail surface.
